label: Comparing a reflective recipient and its giver on the grounds of their own present esse
summary: Holding the question about the constitution and principal of one's own present esse fixed, positive insight into its explanatory essence–esse identity could suffice for the source, while a participant that grasps receipt must still identify its particular principal. Mode recognition alone ties. The expanded answer needs warranted underivedness on the source side. Even granting the very same positive identity leaves a further dispute over whether that identity explains this bearer's obtaining at all, as opposed to its constitution given existence. Immanent primary self-apprehension and present reflective exercise give independent reasons to credit self-access, while neither alone establishes explanatory understanding. The q.44 sole-giver argument supplies a way for an informed recipient to discriminate the right principal if it actually knows and applies the premises. Correct success can therefore tie despite different modes, and access to the explanation can favor the recipient under the converse cognitive assignment. The latter assignment is no evidence of actual source ignorance. See docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md, 'What does a reflective recipient grasp about its own present actuality?', and Scratch/strict-esse-scale/ReflectiveGround.lean. One shared pure determination could be preserved on this pair. A source-only determination could distinguish profiles under inclusion. Neither supplies all-pair preservation, scalar calibration, or an independently justified crossing for all identity-giver pairs. The general adequacy and universal limited/unlimited claims receive no premise discharge.
blocker: The primary-self-object theorem does not show that the source understands the explanatory ratio of its own subsistence. A reflective recipient can identify its principal conditionally. Seek a further explanatory content or degree of comprehension for which there is evidence of differential attainment and a defended link to the whole bearer's degree.
